observed_mechanics: 0x00c472e0-0x00c472e2 PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI establishes a 16-byte register-save frame; there is no SUB ESP and no local storage.
0x00c472e3 MOV ESI,ECX is the only read of the incoming ECX, which fixes the receiver convention as thiscall.
0x00c472e5 MOV EBP,dword ptr [ESI + 0x17c] loads a sub-object pointer; 0x00c472ec TEST EBP,EBP with 0x00c472ee JNZ skips 0x00c472f0, so a null at +0x17c is replaced by the receiver itself.
0x00c472f2 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x9c] and 0x00c472f8 MOV EDI,dword ptr [EAX + 0x13c] chain two loads to reach a leaf object; EDI keeps it for the 0x00c4732a call.
0x00c472fe CALL 0x00c451e0 is issued with ECX untouched since 0x00c472e3, so that port receives the same receiver as this function.
0x00c47305 MOV EBX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x84] reads a dword out of whatever 0x00c451e0 returned, i.e. the cached sub-object, not out of the receiver.

0x00c4730b MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x10c] with EDX loaded from [ESI] at 0x00c47303 is a virtual dispatch through receiver vtable slot +0x10c; 0x00c47311/0x00c47313/0x00c47315 push 0, 0 and the sub-object and 0x00c47316 restores ECX to the receiver, so the call is vslot_0x10c(receiver, sub, 0, 0).
0x00c4731a/0x00c4731d/0x00c47323/0x00c47325 dispatch receiver vtable slot +0xa4 with no stack argument, i.e. vslot_0xa4(receiver).
0x00c47328 MOV ECX,EDI then 0x00c4732a CALL 0x00ce6950 passes the leaf object from 0x00c472f8 as the receiver of a two-instruction getter (MOV EAX,[ECX+0x184]; RET).

0x00b3d4a0 is exactly `MOV EAX,dword ptr [0x0167eb44]` / `RET` (disassembled live), so it consumes no stack word; the Ghidra decompilation that shows FUN_00b3d4a0(uVar6,uVar4) is a stack-model artefact.
0x00c47336 MOV ECX,EAX turns that global into the receiver of 0x00aeb7a0, so the global 0x0167eb44 is the registry the new record is appended to.

0x00aeb7a0 is a one-instruction thunk (JMP 0x00aeb160); 0x00aeb160 ends in RET 0x1c, which pops the 28 bytes of arguments this function pushed, so the seven-argument shape is proved by the callee and not assumed.

Reading 0x00aeb160 backwards from its own frame proves the argument order: after its four register saves and its own `ADD ESP,0x18`, [ESP+0x14..0x2c] are args 1..7, and it stores them to +0x18, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3c, +0x40, +0x44, +0x48 of the new object respectively.

0x00aeb1c3-0x00aeb1d9 show arg5 being treated as a refcounted handle: the previous occupant of +0x40 is released through vtable slot +0x04 and arg5 is then stored, so arg5 is an intrusive reference to the effective mission.
0x00c47338 is reached from 19 sibling SetState-shaped callers, and 0x00c47331's return value is used only as the next call's ECX, never as data.
0x00c472e0 appears nowhere in .rdata or .data as a dword (vtable scan total=0), so it is a non-virtual member and its class is not vtable-proven.

sibling_analysis.question: are 0x00c472e0 and 0x00c471c0 siblings?
sibling_analysis.answer: They do not call each other. Neither is in a vtable. What makes them siblings is that 18 of the 19 canonical callers of 0x00c471c0 are also callers of 0x00c472e0, and in every one of the four fully disassembled callers the call order is always 0x00c472e0 first and 0x00c471c0 last, with the second reached by a tail JMP rather than a CALL.
sibling_analysis.shared_shape: 0x00c4b760, 0x00c63130, 0x00c63170 and 0x00c631b0 are four near-identical functions differing only in the state literal they store (1, 2, 3) and the vtable slot they dispatch first (+0x6c or +0x70). Each stores that literal into the derived state field at +0x1f0, calls 0x00c47d80 when the value changed, then calls 0x00c472e0 and tail-jumps to 0x00c471c0. That is the signature of the tail of a SetState override, and it is what makes these two functions the last two steps of a mission state transition.
sibling_analysis.third_sibling: 0x00c47d80 is called from the same four functions immediately before 0x00c472e0 and clears the two eastl::string16 fields at +0x14c/+0x150 and +0x15c/+0x160 (writing DX at the old buffer and reloading the pointer) and pushes the literal 0x38cf2fd, which equals SimulatorMessages::kMsgMissionUpdate in SimulatorMessages.h:50. cMission.h:54-56 documents exactly that behaviour for SetState.

semantic_contract: Given a mission-like receiver, this function publishes the artifacts of a state transition. 1. It resolves the effective mission: EBP = [this+0x17c], and if that is null EBP is replaced by the receiver itself (0x00c472e5-0x00c472f0). 2. It resolves a second object through the receiver's +0x9c pointer and that object's +0x13c field (0x00c472f2, 0x00c472f8). 3. It asks the receiver for its cached sub-object via 0x00c451e0 and reads the dword at +0x84 of the result (0x00c472fe, 0x00c47305). 4. It calls two of its own virtuals: slot +0x10c with (effective_mission, 0, 0) and slot +0xa4 with no argument (0x00c4730b-0x00c47325). 5. It reads a dword at +0x184 of the object from step 2 (0x00ce6950, 0x00c4732a). 6. It reads the global pointer 0x0167eb44 (0x00b3d4a0, 0x00c47331) and, using that pointer as the receiver, hands all six values plus two explicit zeros to 0x00aeb7a0/0x00aeb160, which allocates a 160-byte record, stores those values at fixed offsets and links the record into the list held by the global, taking an intrusive reference to the effective mission on the way (0x00c47338). Invariants: the function has no branch other than the null-substitution at +0x17c; none of the five intermediate results is tested; the function itself writes nothing in the receiver; the whole argument vector of the final call is built in the order recorded in constants and fields_and_offsets, and the callee pops all 28 bytes so the receiver's own frame is balanced by the four register pops and a bare RET.
classification_rationale: The complete body, ABI, frame, every field offset, every constant, every global, both virtual slots and all five direct callees were read from the disassembly, and the four fully disassembled callers corroborate a single calling shape. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because three material elements stay bounded: (a) OWNING CLASS - the function is non-virtual and no vtable was located, so cMission is a layout-and-neighbourhood candidate, not an established identity; (b) the two dispatched virtual slots have no resolved concrete callee, and the SDK's declared signature for slot +0x10c (no parameters) contradicts the observed three-argument call, so even the slot correspondence is unconfirmed; (c) the class of the 0xa0-byte record built by 0x00aeb160, the meaning of 0x0167eb44 at run time (it is zero in the file image) and the domain meaning of the dword at +0x84 of the cached sub-object are all unestablished.
semantic_findings: The function is the second-to-last step of every mission SetState override in the binary: 18 of its 20 canonical callers also call 0x00c471c0 immediately afterwards, and the four callers that were disassembled in full all follow the pattern store-state-literal / 0x00c47d80 / 0x00c472e0 / tail-JMP 0x00c471c0.

The literal state values stored by those callers are 1, 2 and 3, which match MissionState::Finished, ::Accepted and ::Active in Spore-ModAPI SimulatorEnums.h:265-270, and the message constant pushed by their common helper 0x00c47d80 is 0x38cf2fd, which is SimulatorMessages::kMsgMissionUpdate in SimulatorMessages.h:50. That is four independent agreements between the observed code and one header, which is why cMission is recorded as a candidate rather than dismissed.

The self-substitution idiom at +0x17c is not unique to this function: 0x00c47b96 in a neighbouring function performs the identical null-check-and-copy on the same offset, which is what a shipped mpParentMission idiom compiles to.

The registry port's fifth argument is an intrusive reference, not a raw pointer: 0x00aeb160 releases the previous holder of +0x40 through vtable slot +0x04 before storing the new one and separately calls vtable slot 0 on the same object, which is the AddRef/Release pair that Spore-ModAPI documents for Object-derived types.

0x00b3d4a0 takes no arguments and 0x00ce6950 takes none on the stack, so the Ghidra pseudocode rendering of 0x00c472e0 with two arguments to the former is a stack-modelling artefact; the real seven-argument vector is the one proved by 0x00aeb160's own reads and its RET 0x1c.
This function performs no branch on any of the values it gathers. Every decision it embodies was already made by its callers; it only marshals.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? It is non-virtual and appears in no vtable, so cMission remains a candidate. The 20 callers are SetState overrides of derived mission types, so the receiver is at least a cMission subclass, but which subclass varies per call site and is not determinable statically.

What do the two dispatched virtuals do? Slot +0x10c is called with (mission, 0, 0) and slot +0xa4 with no arguments, and cMission.h suggests GetConversationID at +0xa4 and func10Ch at +0x10c, but the declared func10Ch arity contradicts the call and no vtable was found to confirm either.

What is the 0xa0-byte object that 0x00aeb160 creates from type id 0x13f09b4, and what is the global 0x0167eb44 that owns the list it is appended to? The type id is also used by 0x01046fc0 to build a 0x78-byte Simulator service, so it is not a unique class tag, and the global is zero in the file image.

What does the dword at +0x84 of the object returned by 0x00c451e0 represent? It is forwarded verbatim as the first argument of the registration call and is never tested here, so its domain is entirely the callee's business.

Is 0x0167eb44 guaranteed non-null at the point of use? This function dereferences the result of 0x00b3d4a0 into ECX without a null check, so a null registry would fault inside 0x00aeb160. No static evidence establishes that the global is initialised first.
What is at mission offset +0x130 and why does only the sibling 0x00c471c0 read it? Recorded because the two functions are otherwise tightly coupled, but not part of this function's contract.
Is the +0x184 read on the +0x13c leaf a field or the start of a nested object? Only one dword is consumed and 0x00ce6950 exposes nothing further.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for 0x00c472e0. The classification rests entirely on static reads of SporeApp.exe 3.1.0.22.

A runtime differential test would be needed to confirm the runtime value of 0x0167eb44, the number of records the registry accumulates across a mission transition, and that no runtime patch retargets the two virtual slots.
The concrete overrides reached through slots +0x10c and +0xa4 can only be named by observing a receiver whose vtable base is known at run time.
